title: AB 325 Cartwright Act: Common Pricing Algorithm Restrictions
requirement: The Cartwright Act prohibits using or distributing common pricing algorithms as part of a conspiracy to restrain trade or coerce users into adopting pricing recommendations.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies generally to persons using or distributing common pricing algorithms to restrain trade or coerce prices.

exemptions: Does not include the end consumer of a product or service.
citation: AB-325 / Business and Professions Code Section 16729
quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
(b) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.

coverage.summary: Applies generally to persons using or distributing common pricing algorithms to restrain trade or coerce prices.

supporting_sources.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.

title: Application Fee Cap
requirement: Landlords and their agents cannot charge a residential rental application or screening fee exceeding $50, subject to annual CPI adjustments.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to residential rental properties generally, with explicit exemptions for one-family or two-family dwellings offered for rent and real estate licensees who are not the landlord.

exemptions: One-family or two-family dwellings offered for rent; a licensee of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission unless the licensee is the landlord.

agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply

exceeds $50.

title: Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Rent Control Exemption
requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to newly constructed multiple dwellings.

interaction: May preempt the listed local rules once in force; every affected address is flagged for human review rather than decided.

title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - Criminal Record Screening Limitations
requirement: Housing providers are prohibited from inquiring about or considering an applicant's criminal record prior to issuing a conditional offer of rental housing, with limited exceptions.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to rental dwelling units in New Jersey, excluding dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
coverage_conditions.owner_condition: owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are exempt

exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
quoted_span:
A
housing provider
shall not require an applicant to
complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding an
applicant’s criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer,
except that a housing provider may consider whether an applicant has ever been
convicted of drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production
of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether
the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State
sex offender registration program.

title: Maximum Security Deposit Limit
requirement: Landlords are prohibited from charging a security deposit exceeding one and one-half times one month's rent, and must return the deposit within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy.

coverage_conditions.summary: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes, excluding owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless requested by tenant.

exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings
